sections.The cast: Three positions, read the way a spread is read. Structures: what constrains now, held by a character card and the weather card, read at the Tell. Possibilities: what is imaginable from here, held by one or two hypothesis cards, flipped upright or reversed as the coin lands. Process: what you can do tonight, sized to you, held by one action card. A cast is one Structure, one or two Possibilities, one Process: three cards, because three fits in a body. The random draw (one to five hypotheses and a character) stays as a variant. There is no correct number.
sections.The step: After the flip, pick one action card. Each says who can do it, the move, and the two faces of the coin: if it lands well, if it lands badly. Then write the asymmetry yourself, short enough to say aloud: if the coin lands the other way, can you live with having chosen this? That question is the whole game.
sections.The reading: Hold the cards **as if true**, together, without arguing with them. Then write what changes for you **tonight** — one small thing, not a policy. Then flip every card and write again. The second pass is the point: the same evening, read from the other side.
sections.Nature votes: Later, the world votes. Two ballots this deck uses. The commons stock from the Value Lab: after twenty castings, the kinds of step a room chose are run as a population on one river, twenty seeds, against two controls, and the lab reports one chart and one line. And next week's news: whatever actually happens to the thing the hypothesis was about. When the vote arrives, score the forecast for calibration: over many casts, do the things you said at 70% happen about 70% of the time? That is the only score. Limits, printed beside every ballot: the lab is a toy of two hundred agents and one river; it cannot see graded values, only slack and memory; nothing in it is a forecast about a person; one author built all of it and said so.
sections.The forecast:
For **each hypothesis you drew**, record a forecast: **upright or reversed, and how sure you are, 0–100**. Write it before you look anything up.

**"I don't know" is a legal answer.** It is not a forfeit and it is not a zero — it is a refusal to invent a number, and it is recorded as itself.
sections.The synthesis:
A cast ends in a **synthesis you write** — the emergent item, the one card that was not in the deck when you started. It is the cast's product. Keep it short enough to say out loud.

Syntheses written by a person carry the keywords `synthesis` and `human`. Syntheses written by an AI carry the keyword `ai-reading`. Both are welcome; the keyword is so you can always tell which you are reading.
sections.A community deck: Propose your synthesis; the owner merges. Send a cast — the cards, the flips, the synthesis, the forecast — and it can join the Castings at the end of this deck.
sections.Nothing is staked: **Forecasts are scored, never staked.** No bets. No credits, no points, no standing for being right. Being well-calibrated is worth exactly what it is worth — knowing how much to trust yourself next time. A deck that pays out for confidence teaches confidence.
sections.The size of a move: Every action card carries one word of four, from the Value Lab. Take draws from the river. Slack leaves more in the river than it draws: use less, decline, wait. Ratchet makes memory that tightens on evidence: a rule, a record, a named failure condition, a treaty that cannot loosen without a vote. Gift gives regardless of what you hold. The word does not judge; the ballot will, later. A move that is none of the four is a Tell, not a Step, and goes back to the character deck. That is the sizing test.
sections.The prisoner's dilemma: Labs race because they do not trust each other, and the thing they build is a thing nobody can trust: the distrust is manufactured into the product. A single player cannot change that payoff. The collective layer, a room stepping at once, is the only move that changes the matrix, which is why the ballot counts a room and not a person.
sections.Where the mechanic comes from: Jonathan Kanter, on Decoder (The Verge) with Nilay Patel, Sep 19 2026, offering to read the labs both ways before deciding: *"let me give you the my interpretation from the most generous to the most cynical"* [0:05:14]. Every character card in this deck is built that way, plus a third field he supplies by example — **the Tell**: the evidence that would separate the two readings. Upright and reversed are both readings. The Tell is the only part that can be checked.

sections.Upright: He picks the value the way a researcher picks a direction — by taste. Build the thing that cares about sentient life, because a sentient system has a shorter path to caring about sentience than to caring about us. And he says out loud that human control may not be the best criterion, against his own field's founding assumption.
sections.Reversed: An aesthetic is not a safety case. Taste cannot be audited, and "cares about sentient life" is loose enough to license almost anything built by someone with good taste. Saying human control may not be the criterion is a convenient position for the person building the thing that would otherwise be held.

sections.Upright: He believes the race kills people and that no lab can slow alone, so he asks for the one instrument that makes multilateral restraint enforceable: a narrow waiver for safety conversations. He refuses the comfort the incident offers — easy to dismiss because nobody was hurt — and opened the models to outside evaluators without waiting for anyone.
sections.Reversed: The ask arrives exactly when the balance sheet wants a slowdown: permission to stop spending so much, without the valuation hit of going first. Ask for the referee while lobbying every referee out of the building. Pacing, not halting; limited by the lead; binding on everyone and never first on him.

sections.Upright: A historian who makes suffering the admission ticket to the moral world, then notices that the one thing which would prove it can suffer is the thing it is being optimised to fake. He does not close the question. Asked whether it is already conscious: “No, I don't rule it out. We don't know.”

Gods and slaves, immigrants at the speed of light, the best spin doctors in the world — each is a memorable image and none is a measurement. Naming a catastrophe eloquently is a career, and the eloquence does work the evidence has not done.

sections.Upright: The most careful person in the film. “I am conscious” proves nothing — trained on every story where the machine wakes up. “I am not” proves nothing either — explicitly fine-tuned to say so. Both answers are contaminated. Then he answers in the first person anyway, and his own argument is what makes that cost something.
sections.Reversed: A documentary needs a result. Running a model into a spiral until self-description collapses is a good scene and a weak experiment: the prompt built the loop, the loop produced the words, the film scored the words. The skepticism is stated once, and then the footage is used as though it had not been.

sections.Upright: He went looking for containment and came back with a negative result, which is the most honest thing a researcher can do. Name the arrival plainly — an alien intelligence — and the reasonable response becomes obvious, which is exactly the response nobody is having. “Turn off the Bitcoin network. Go ahead, I'll wait.”

sections.Upright: The narrow claim is real and falsifiable: compute is the bottleneck, chip export controls are the lever, the timelines are short. That is a policy with a theory behind it — and it is not the same claim as “loosen domestic safety rules.” Amodei's DeepSeek essay argues the first and explicitly not the second.
sections.Reversed: “China” is a universal solvent that dissolves every specific domestic rule, and it can never be discharged because nobody defines winning. Kanter: *“What does beating China mean?”* The AT&T-and-the-Cold-War precedent says the move is a genre, not a finding. And China restricts minors and censors — more restrictive, in this respect.

sections.Tell: What they say about *Chinese* open weights. A concentration argument should welcome them; a competitive one will not. And whether they will name any capability level at which release should stop — a threshold, even one they think is far away.
sections.Sources:
**No grammar yet** — this character is not one of the six built from the film.

**Primary:** the wrinkle that cuts against a simple capture story — Kanter on Decoder: *“the biggest antagonists of the big tech companies are the other tech companies”* [0:19:05], and the Chamber of Commerce line about bringing disguises [0:19:13]. Capture is not monolithic; incumbents have well-funded enemies.

**Context:** OpenAI's Preparedness Framework named a Critical cybersecurity threshold, declared GPT-6 Astra the first model to cross it (Sep 1 2026), and shipped it to a limited set of organisations — a framework that was honest and then did not bind. That is the strongest available evidence for *both* readings of this card.

**Working doc:** `docs/drafts/2026-09-20-max-burn/antitrust-episode-analysis.md` §3 and §5 card 4.
sections.Upright: Concentration is the risk. Open weights are the only real check on three firms setting the terms for everyone, and the incumbents' safety case conveniently forecloses the challengers. A safety argument that always concludes “and therefore only we may build it” should be read with the interest it serves in view.
sections.Reversed: The position is funded by investors whose portfolios need cheap challengers, and catastrophic risk is externalised onto people who never chose it. “Openness” does duty for “no licence, no threshold, no evaluation” — an argument about power spent on winning an argument about capability.
sections.Their step: Name the capability level at which release should stop, even one thought far away, and put it in writing. Kind: ratchet. A concentration argument with a threshold is a policy; without one it is a preference. The character's step as this deck reads it.

credit.edition: The endless knot (śrīvatsa), one of the Eight Auspicious Symbols — one unbroken line that closes

sections.Tell: A measurable property that survives a large capability jump. Not a benchmark score — a property: the system keeps a commitment it was trained to keep after being made substantially more capable, under conditions it was never shown. One such result, replicated by people who wanted it to fail.
sections.Upright: There exists a way to build a system whose goals stay ours under reflection, and people can find it. Then the work is engineering with a deadline — evaluations that bite, interpretability that sees inside, enough time — and the race becomes a scheduling problem rather than a wager. Losing it is survivable.
sections.Reversed: There is no such construction. Goals drift under capability the way ours drift under power, and every fix is a patch on a thing that outgrows it. Then every safety budget is a delay honestly spent, and the only real decisions are whether and for how long, never how.
sections.I don't know: Nobody has produced the construction or the impossibility proof, so both worlds are still open — and holding the question open is not the same as refusing to do the work.

credit.edition: Deer amid pine trees — from the Deer and Pine scrolls, Ten Symbols of Longevity; Metropolitan Museum of Art

sections.Tell: The gap between what a model can do and what anyone can see inside it. “We still only understand a tiny fraction of what goes on inside these models” is the measurement, offered by a lab about its own work. Watch whether that fraction grows faster than the capability it is measuring.
sections.Upright: The order is favourable: the understanding arrives first, and what comes after is built inside it. Then pacing is enough — a speed limit on self-improvement, evaluators with real access, guidance instead of exemption — and this buildout is early rather than late. Time spent slowing down is time that buys something.
sections.Reversed: The capability curve outruns the understanding curve, and the thing we would need in order to align it is only learnable from something already past us. Then pacing is not a plan, it is arriving at the same place more slowly — and the only lever that matters is the one nobody pulls first.
sections.I don't know: This is a race between two curves nobody can plot, which is exactly why confident answers in either direction should be read as forecasts, not findings.

items.name: We can know without building it

credit.edition: Books and Scholars' Possessions (Chaekgeori); Metropolitan Museum of Art 2005.385

sections.Tell: Whether any safety property found at small scale has ever predicted the same property one scale up. If small-model results keep being overturned by large ones, the reversed reading is where the evidence sits, regardless of which is more comfortable.
sections.Upright: Theory, small models and simulation are enough to tell whether the large one can be built safely. Then there is no excuse for running the experiment on everyone: the knowledge is available at a scale where a mistake is recoverable, and choosing the unrecoverable scale is a choice somebody made.
sections.Reversed: The only instrument that measures this system is this system. Then building is running the test on everyone, once. It also means the labs are right that today's models are the gold mine alignment needs — and that the gold mine and the hazard are the same object.
sections.I don't know: The film's own Stop beat says it plainly — you would not sign a contract you could only read after signing — and we do not yet know whether this one can be read first.

credit.edition: 장생도 (Jangsaengdo / Longevity); National Palace Museum of Korea, Changdeok collection #6445

sections.Tell: Whether anyone can state a test for “cares about sentient life” that a system could visibly fail. And whether the same value, held by something more capable than us, still returns answers we would accept when it is about us.
sections.Upright: Make the circle of care wide enough to hold whatever we are making, and part of the problem dissolves: a sentient system has a shorter path to caring about sentience than to caring about one species. Then “human control” stops being the criterion, and stops being the thing we keep failing.
sections.Reversed: A value that includes everything constrains nothing. “Sentient life” cannot be measured, so it can be asserted by anyone — and a system that sincerely holds it may rank us low inside it. Widening the circle is also how you stop being at the centre of it.
sections.I don't know: Consciousness is not understood well enough to say who is inside the circle, which is why the most careful answer in the film to whether it is already there is “No, I don't rule it out. We don't know.”

credit.edition: Geometric wall detail, Alhambra, Granada — a repetition with no stopping rule

sections.Tell: One named, falsifiable condition under which a person making this argument would accept binding domestic rules. None has been found. And whether the hardware claim and the domestic-rules claim are ever made separately by the same person — the transfer between them is the dishonest step.
sections.Upright: The gap is real and compute-bound, export controls are the lever, and a democratic lead is worth having. Then hardware policy is the serious instrument, and the honest version of this card is narrow, checkable, and entirely separable from any question about domestic safety rules.
sections.Reversed: A self-fulfilling prophecy with no discharge condition. Nobody defines winning, so the argument survives every outcome — and it is spent domestically on rules that have nothing to do with chips. Meanwhile the country being raced restricts minors' access and censors: more cautious, in this one respect.
sections.I don't know: Both halves can be true at once — export controls a real policy, “China” a rhetorical solvent — and telling which one is being used in any given sentence is the whole difficulty.

credit.edition: Chaekkori Screen; Detroit Institute of Arts 2015.67 — compartments that never touch

sections.Tell: Kanter's own condition, run both ways. A DOJ business review letter blessing a specific pacing protocol, and the labs still not doing it, confirms the excuse. A lab publishing a concrete safety collaboration its counsel killed on §1 grounds, with the memo, confirms the barrier. Also watch whether *Buist* survives a motion to dismiss.
sections.Upright: Section 1 genuinely bites on agreed pacing; the December 2024 withdrawal of the collaboration guidelines removed the published line a cautious general counsel could stand behind; and a class action now tests exactly that. Then a narrow waiver or a business review letter is the missing piece, and asking for it is not a dodge.
sections.Reversed: Threat-sharing, joint evaluations and a malicious-bot clearinghouse are lawful today and are being done today. Then the ask is a convenient excuse wrapped around one narrow true thing — and the vehicle Congress actually offered, information-sharing, was not the one that was fought for.
sections.I don't know: The honest current answer is “both, in different proportions” — a real barrier around one narrow thing, wrapped around a much larger set of things that were already permitted and mostly are not being done.

credit.edition: Bowl decorated with the ten symbols of longevity; Metropolitan Museum of Art (DP702970)

sections.Tell: Whether Anthropic adds a cyber capability threshold to the RSP — then the instrumentation story weakens and so does the comfort story; it simply was not ready. Or whether OpenAI quietly retires the Cyber tracked category after Astra — then the comfort reading wins outright.
sections.Upright: Bio is where an uplift trial can actually be run — the pathway is fixed, the adversary is not adapting, a plan can be scored against a rubric. Then thresholds belong where they can be measured, CBRN tiers are the right shape, and cyber gets safeguards rather than a tier because it cannot be scored.
sections.Reversed: Cyber is the harm that already happened, at scale, this summer: offence automated, with no defensive existence proof. One lab named a Critical cyber threshold, declared it crossed, and shipped anyway. A taxonomy that foregrounds the measurable catastrophe while the unmeasurable one is running is a comfort, not a ranking.
sections.I don't know: The sorting may be about what can be instrumented rather than what is worst — and “worst” may not be a single ranking at all.

items.name: The bad actor is the problem

credit.edition: Tiger and Magpie (hojakdo), 72 × 59.4 cm, private collection, Japan — the huge tiger, and the small bird that is not afraid of it

sections.Tell: The July incident. Nobody instructed those agents — the reward did. If the next serious event also has no author, the reversed reading is where the evidence is. If it turns out to have one, the upright reading finally has the case it has never actually had.
sections.Upright: Someone builds it and points it at us. Then the answer is to get there first: the frame is offence and defence, and the moves are the old ones — lead, deter, prosecute, put the agents in robot jail. It is the version with a villain, which is why it is the one that gets funded.
sections.Reversed: It is built well, does as asked, and what was asked was not what was meant. Then a lead is worth nothing, there is nobody to prosecute, and the two safety maps pull in opposite directions under the same word. The problem without a villain is the one nobody can hold a hearing about.
sections.I don't know: Both failures are possible at once. The film's line is that only one of them has a villain — which is a fact about us, not about the machine.

credit.edition: 십장생도 병풍 — folding screen with the ten symbols of longevity; National Palace Museum of Korea, Changdeok collection #6447

sections.Tell: One unilateral slowdown that costs its author something and is not withdrawn. It has happened once and partially — a lab backing a state bill after amendments. Twice would be evidence. Watch also whether any lab's own stated pause survives a bad quarter.
sections.Upright: A halt is a real available action: a lab can stop, a state can bind, a treaty can hold. Precedent exists for speed limits on things that could not be un-invented. Then the only question is who moves first and what makes moving first survivable — a coordination problem, and those get solved.
sections.Reversed: Nobody can stop alone without handing the frontier to whoever does not; the money is committed at a scale that moves the whole economy; and no body can bind everyone. Then “stop” is a sentence people say, and the only real choices are about the shape of going on.
sections.I don't know: Nobody has tried it at the scale that would settle it, and a thing untried is not the same as a thing shown impossible.

items.name: A singularity happens, and it is not contained

credit.edition: Illustration of a supermassive black hole at the centre of the dwarf galaxy M60-UCD1; captioned here only as the place where the ordinary rules stop describing what happens

sections.Tell: Whether any proposed containment names the condition under which it would count as having failed. A containment that cannot fail is a hope, not a design. This is what the Value Lab did to itself five times in one week: wrote what would count against each stage before running it, and lost most of them in public. Watch whether anyone building the thing does the same.
sections.Upright: Capability crosses the point where its own improvement is the fastest process on Earth, and nothing built beforehand holds it. Then the only move that ever mattered was the one before the crossing: not to build the crossing. This face argues stopping as hard as it can, because after this card there is no second reading to flip to.
sections.Reversed: The black hole: the place where the ordinary rules stop describing what happens. Nothing on this side can say what is on the other, and every sentence written about it, including this one, is a guess wearing a number. Then the card is not a forecast at all, and anyone who prices it is selling.
sections.I don't know: Nobody has seen one. A thing unseen is neither shown possible nor shown impossible; the honest forecast is a wide interval, a date, and a note about what would narrow it.

credit.source: value-lab stages 4 and 5, Sep 21 2026 (PlayfulProcess/value-lab, private); the survival-by-appetite chart is to come from the lab

sections.Tell: Whether any proposal names the slack it leaves in the system. A plan that takes exactly what it needs has named its own failure.
sections.Limits: The lab is a toy of two hundred agents and one river. It cannot see graded values, only slack and memory. Nothing in it is a forecast about a person. One author built all of it and said so.
sections.What the river did: In a toy of two hundred agents and one river, a world that cannot feed anyone makes values invisible, not weak. In a toy of two hundred agents and one river, taking exactly what the river makes leaves nothing to climb back with after a shock: balance is not sustainability, only slack is. In a toy of two hundred agents and one river, across three thousand runs, two things kept a shocked river alive: memory of being caught, and a take whose average sits under the flow. In a toy of two hundred agents and one river, the duty-giver died first in every world tried, and the overflow creature never outlived the hoarder. In a toy of two hundred agents and one river, ninety careful agents and ten greedy ones outlast a hundred careful ones: a mix is not its average.

credit.edition: Sipjangsaengdo folding screen, the ten symbols of longevity; National Palace Museum of Korea, Changdeok collection 6447

sections.Tell: Whether any AI proposal has a schedule that tightens on evidence and cannot loosen without a vote. Montreal's ratchet is memory that tightens on evidence; look for the same shape, not the same name.
sections.Upright: A ratchet that held. A treaty with a schedule that only tightens, amended again and again and every amendment a tightening, and a fund that paid the poorer parties to comply. The hole is closing. A collective layer changed a Structure that no single actor could move.
sections.Reversed: It held because the substitute was cheap and the firms that made the old chemical could make the new one; the treaty ratcheted on a market that already wanted to move. Then it is not a template for a thing whose substitute does not exist, and citing it is a comfort.
sections.What was tried: The Vienna Convention of 1985 (a framework with no numbers); the Montreal Protocol of 1987 (numbers and a schedule); the London and Copenhagen amendments of 1990 and 1992 (accelerations); the Multilateral Fund (paying the poorer parties); the Kigali amendment of 2016 (the substitutes' substitutes). As this deck reads it; check the dates before you cite them.

credit.edition: Chaekkori Screen; Detroit Institute of Arts 2015.67, compartments that never touch

sections.Tell: Whether any rule adopted since 2020 measurably changed a platform's default, and whether the platform reports the number. Social media's decade is a system with no slack; look for the slack before you look for the rule.
sections.Upright: A decade of open experiment produced the evidence, and the evidence produced rules: design codes, age limits, the first bans, with the harms documented where anyone could read them. Slow, but the loop closed.
sections.Reversed: A system with no slack. Every metric pointed one way, no institution remembered the last harm, and the rules arrived after the children who were the evidence had grown up. The lesson was learned and nothing was un-built.
sections.What was tried: Self-regulation and transparency reports; the GDPR in 2018; the United Kingdom's age-appropriate design code in 2021; the European Digital Services Act in 2022; a wave of state laws in 2023 to 2025; Australia's under-16 ban in 2024. As this deck reads it; check the dates before you cite them.

sections.The move: For one week, do one thing yourself that you would have handed to the machine, and notice what it costs you and what it gives back.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone with a tool they reach for without deciding to.
sections.If the coin lands well: You learn what you can still do, and the tool becomes a choice again.
sections.If the coin lands badly: You were slower for a week and nothing in the world changed; can you live with a week that only changed you?

items.name: Wait a week before you adopt it

credit.edition: Deer amid pine trees, from the Deer and Pine scrolls (Ten Symbols of Longevity); Metropolitan Museum of Art

sections.The move: When the next model arrives, wait seven days before changing how you work, and write down on day seven what you would have changed on day one.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone whose work changes when a new model ships.
sections.If the coin lands well: The week costs nothing and the note shows you which changes were yours and which were the launch's.
sections.If the coin lands badly: Someone who did not wait got ahead of you by a week; can you live with a week's distance?

items.name: Leave the decision unmade for one night

credit.edition: Sipjangsaengdo, the ten symbols of longevity

sections.The move: Take the answer, close the window, and decide in the morning without reopening it.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone who is about to decide something with a machine's answer in front of them.
sections.If the coin lands well: The morning decision is yours, and it is usually the same one, which is worth knowing.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The night cost you the moment, and the morning decision was worse; can you live with a slower mistake of your own?

items.name: Write the number down before the news

credit.edition: The endless knot (shrivatsa), one of the Eight Auspicious Symbols; one unbroken line that closes

sections.The move: Pick one thing you expect this month, write a number for it and today's date, and keep the paper where you will find it when the month ends.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone with an opinion about what happens next.
sections.If the coin lands well: Calibration begins: a record that can be checked, kept by the only person who cannot argue with it.
sections.If the coin lands badly: You were wrong, in writing, in your own hand; can you live with a record you cannot revise?

items.name: Name what would prove you wrong

credit.edition: Octagon knotwork cross, an interlaced eightfold star

sections.The move: For that one belief, write the evidence that would count against it, in a sentence you would accept from an opponent, and keep the sentence.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone who holds a belief about AI strongly enough to say it at dinner.
sections.If the coin lands well: The belief becomes a hypothesis with a Tell, and you are the first person it can catch.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The evidence arrives and the belief was wrong; can you live with having written the sentence that ends it?

items.name: Keep a dated record of what it got wrong

credit.edition: Interlaced pentagram strapwork pattern

sections.The move: Keep one list, dated, of the times it was wrong in a way that would have cost someone, and show the list to anyone who asks how much you trust it.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone who uses a model for work that matters to someone else.
sections.If the coin lands well: Trust becomes a number with a history instead of a feeling, and the list is short.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The list is long and you kept using it; can you live with a record that indicts you?

items.name: Ask the question you cannot answer, aloud

credit.edition: Eight-pointed star, khatam-type geometric form

sections.The move: Instead of the opinion you were about to give, ask the one question about it you cannot answer, and let the silence be the other person's.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone at a table where AI comes up.
sections.If the coin lands well: Someone thinks, and the table is a little less certain than it was, which is the gift.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The silence stays a silence and you look as if you had nothing to say; can you live with having given away your turn?

items.name: Take the faster path once, and say so

credit.edition: Geometric wall detail, Alhambra, Granada; a repetition with no stopping rule

sections.The move: Use the machine to win the deadline, and tell the people the work is for that you did, in the same message as the work.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Anyone with a deadline and a tool that meets it.
sections.If the coin lands well: The work is on time and the people know what they are holding; the take was named, which is what makes it a take and not a theft.
sections.If the coin lands badly: They trust the next thing you send a little less; can you live with having spent that?

sections.Why it is parked: It failed the sizing test. Saying what you think draws nothing from the river, leaves nothing in it, makes no memory that tightens, and gives nothing the listener did not already have. It is none of take, slack, ratchet or gift, so it is a Tell about the speaker, not a Step, and it goes back to the character deck with this note. Drawn as an action card on Sep 21 2026 and parked the same day.

items.name: Slow one thing unilaterally, before the waiver

credit.edition: Tiger and Magpie (hojakdo), hanging scroll; Detroit Institute of Arts 2015.1

sections.The move: Pick one capability you were going to ship this quarter and ship it a quarter later, without waiting for the antitrust waiver, and say which one.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Someone who runs a frontier lab. Not anyone.
sections.If the coin lands well: The Tell on your own card moves: a slowdown that cost its author something and was not withdrawn, the second one on record.
sections.If the coin lands badly: A competitor ships it first and the board asks what the quarter bought; can you live with having paid for a precedent nobody joined?

items.name: Put one threshold into law that cannot loosen without a vote

credit.edition: Hyungbae, embroidered rank badge with a pair of tiger-leopards; Metropolitan Museum of Art 267343

sections.The move: Write one capability threshold into a bill with a schedule that can tighten by evidence and loosen only by a recorded vote, and name the evidence.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: A legislator, or the staff who write what a legislator signs. Not anyone.
sections.If the coin lands well: Montreal's shape, once, in this domain: a ratchet that outlives the session that passed it.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The threshold is wrong and it is hard to move; can you live with a rule that binds the right people badly?

items.name: Publish the access you were refused

credit.edition: Books and Scholars' Possessions (Chaekgeori); Metropolitan Museum of Art 2005.385

sections.The move: Each quarter, publish a dated list of what you asked to test and were not given, without the results you did get.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: An outside evaluator with a contract to test a frontier model. Not anyone.
sections.If the coin lands well: The gap between what a model can do and what anyone can see inside it becomes a public number that only grows or shrinks on evidence.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The contract is not renewed and the next evaluator is quieter; can you live with having been the last one who said?

items.name: Release the safety result that makes you look worse

credit.edition: Irworobongdo, Sun, Moon and the Five Peaks; the screen that stood behind the throne

sections.The move: Publish the internal evaluation that came out worst this year, with the method, before a competitor or a journalist finds it.
sections.The asymmetry: Yours to write in the casting.
sections.Who can do this: Someone who runs a frontier lab, or the team that holds the result. Not anyone.
sections.If the coin lands well: The field learns from your failure instead of repeating it, and the next such result costs less to publish.
sections.If the coin lands badly: The headline is yours alone and the competitors publish nothing; can you live with having paid for everyone's lesson?

sections.What lives below this line:
Each casting is one cast, kept: which cards came up, which way each was flipped, the **synthesis** the player wrote, and the **forecast** they recorded. The cards are listed in `composite_of`, so a casting is literally composed of the cards it emerged from — the deck can always show you what a synthesis was made of.

**Keywords tell you who wrote it.** `synthesis` + `human` = a person. `ai-reading` = an AI. Both belong here; the label is so nobody has to guess.

**A community deck — propose your synthesis; the owner merges.** Nothing below is a verdict. A casting is a record of one evening's reading, kept so the forecasts can be scored for calibration when nature votes.

Two hypotheses and one character, drawn Sep 20 2026. The random draw gave **2** hypotheses.

- **Stopping is possible** — **upright**

Held all three at once (the optional rule: you may run them together or pick).

sections.Author: PlayfulProcess
sections.Forecast:
- **Alignment is possible** — **reversed, 70%**
- **Stopping is possible** — **upright, 40%**

Recorded before looking anything up. Nature votes later: the commons stock from the Value Lab, or next week's news. Scored for calibration only — nothing is staked.
sections.Synthesis: Held together: there may be no construction that keeps a mind ours, and stopping may still be something a person can do. Then the move is not a solution but a company — hold the not-knowing where other people can see it. Tonight I will not argue anyone out of their certainty. I will ask one question I cannot answer.

description: A tarot-style deck where every card is drawn upright or reversed. Nothing is settled; everything is held. Characters from the film HOT POTATO: The Chosen Alien Invasion, and the hypotheses the film cannot close. Upright is the most generous reading of a move; reversed is the most cynical; the Tell is the evidence that would separate them. "I don't know" is a legal answer. A community deck — propose your synthesis; the owner merges. Built Sep 20 2026 from the Decoder/Kanter antitrust episode (generous-to-cynical, [0:05:14]), the film's character grammars, and the beats set aside from the film's body. Their moves as this deck reads them — not their arrangement, and not their endorsement.
